# Arbitrarily large midpoint-defect stars with globally small caps

This is an exact limitation of the volume-increasing forest from
`candidate 68ce947b8ac91d32`.
Every edge has the stated strict growth. Nevertheless neither its
indegree nor the total volume at incoming sources is bounded by a
dimension-only multiple of its destination volume. This remains true
for actual globally noheavy convex bodies and caps whose entire mixed
mass is strictly below the OC threshold.

The caps below do not cover the source and do not satisfy an asserted
global criticality condition. This is not an OC counterexample or a
refutation of an argument that uses additional critical-cover data.

## 1. An actual rational cone in every continuous dimension d>=2

Fix integers d>=2 and L>=2, and set N=40dL. Define

    C={ (z,x): -N<=z<=0,
                   0<=x_l<=1+z/N for l=1,...,d }.

All defining constraints are affine. Thus C is a compact convex body
in R times R^d. Its integer fibers, writing k=z+N, are

    C_z=(k/N)[0,1]^d,  k=0,1,...,N.

Only the bottom fiber is null for d-volume. The mixed measure is
therefore H_d, its total mass is

    M=sum_(k=0)^N (k/N)^d,

and its largest fiber, at z=0, has volume one. The increasing
Riemann-sum inequality gives

    M>=integral_0^N (t/N)^d dt=N/(d+1)>2.

Consequently EVERY individual fiber has volume strictly less than
M/2. No global heavy-fiber exception is present.

Choose the 2L distinct source bases

    i_j=-N/2+j,  j=1,...,2L,
    c_j=1+i_j/N=1/2+j/N.

Their opposite endpoint bases are 2i_j=-N+2j, and their common
destination base is zero. All these endpoint fibers have positive
volume. Their actual volume roots are

    (1+2i_j/N, c_j, 1)=(2j/N,c_j,1),

and midpoint compatibility holds with equality. Also

    1/2<c_j<=1/2+1/(20d)<=21/40.                    (1)

## 2. One genuine oblique cap for every edge

Let Gamma=Gamma_d and define

    beta_j=(1-Gamma)c_j,
    H_j={ (z,x): x_1-2(z-i_j)>=beta_j }.

At its source fiber z=i_j the captured fraction is exactly Gamma,
because x_1 is uniform on [0,c_j] under uniform volume in the cube.
Every integer fiber z<=i_j-1 is fully captured: the left side is
at least two, whereas beta_j<1. Every fiber z>=i_j+1 is strictly
missed: its left side is at most 1-2=-1. Thus, in particular, the
opposite endpoint at 2i_j is fully captured and the common endpoint
at zero is fully residual. The three residual roots are exactly

    (0, c_j(1-Gamma)^(1/d), 1).                      (2)

The row fails strictly. For a fully rational comparison of its
sign, ordinary binomial estimates give Gamma>1/3. Concavity of
x^(1/d), or its tangent at x=1, gives

    (1-Gamma)^(1/d)<=1-Gamma/d<1-1/(3d).

Using (1),

    2c_j(1-Gamma)^(1/d)
      <(1+1/(10d))(1-1/(3d))
       =1-7/(30d)-1/(30d^2)<1.

Hence the original midpoint inequality for (2) is false, and every
edge points from i_j to the same destination zero. The endpoint
volume increase and local heaviness are exactly those required by
the proved forest theorem.

For completeness, Gamma>1/3 follows from
(1+1/d)^d<sum_(k=0)^infinity 1/k!<3; the latter strict estimate
follows from 1/k!<=2^(1-k) for k>=2, with strict inequality for
k>=3. These estimates introduce no numerical conjecture.

## 3. Every cap has total mass below the OC budget

Put m_j=N+i_j=N/2+j, so c_j=m_j/N. The full/empty statuses above
give the exact total cap mass

    mu(H_j)=sum_(k=0)^(m_j-1)(k/N)^d+Gamma c_j^d.

Since the function t^d is increasing, its left Riemann sum gives

    mu(H_j)<=N c_j^(d+1)/(d+1)+Gamma c_j^d.

Divide by M>=N/(d+1), use c_j<=21/40, d>=2, Gamma<1/2, and
N=40dL>=30(d+1). Then

    mu(H_j)/M
       <=c_j^(d+1)+Gamma(d+1)/N
       <(21/40)^3+1/60
       =30983/192000
       <1/6<Gamma/2.                               (3)

Thus the selected caps satisfy a GLOBAL strict below-OC budget,
in addition to having the requisite small own-fiber captured fraction.
Closed boundaries do not affect these computations: the continuous
normal is nonzero, so every positive fiber has null hyperplane
boundary, and the only null fiber contributes zero H_d mass.

## 4. Unbounded multiplicity, and the exact scope of the obstruction

There are 2L distinct failing source rows pointing to one destination
of volume one. Their total source-fiber volume satisfies

    sum_(j=1)^(2L) |C_(i_j)|
       =sum_(j=1)^(2L)c_j^d>2L/2^d.

For every fixed d this tends to infinity with L. Therefore neither
a bound on indegree nor a bound on total incoming source mass by a
dimension-only multiple of destination mass follows from:

* actual convex-compatible integer fibers;
* strict global noheavy;
* the original midpoint-row failure;
* own cap fraction at most Gamma_d;
* global cap mass below Gamma_d M/2; and
* strict volume growth along every oriented edge.

All selected caps miss the fiber at zero, so they do not form a
cover. A future global forest argument must exploit additional
coupling, capacity, disjointness, or critical-cover constraints.
The example identifies a precise missing requirement; it does not
invalidate the local sharp threshold or its termination conclusion.
